A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Planning Neural Operator work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and sufficiently complete to match retained, revised, and added content.

before.justification: V1 reports original GridWorld, MovingAI, and iGibson experiments, plus evaluations of PNO-based planning heuristics and obstacle erosion in Sections 4–5 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds hybrid-loss experiments, P-NTFields comparisons, and simulated 4-DOF manipulator results.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a hybrid training-loss variant combining value-function error with a weighted Eikonal gradient-residual penalty in Eq. 15. This refines training while retaining the learned SDF, obstacle encoding, Deepnorm projection, and heuristic procedure. Expanded layer formulas otherwise clarify the existing architecture.

E1.justification: V2 adds planning for an OpenManipulator-X robot in four-dimensional joint configuration space, with randomized workspace obstacles, in Section 4 and Appendix D.5. This substantially extends task coverage beyond the retained grid, city-map, and 3D building navigation experiments.

E2.justification: P-NTFields is added to the Bolton and Samuel iGibson comparisons, with numerical errors, inference times, and path visualizations in Figure 3. Existing comparators remain. Relabeling FNO and DAFNO as PNO component ablations does not introduce additional comparison methods.

E3.justification: The new manipulator experiment introduces a 17^4 configuration-space grid, 40 training maps and 10 test maps with 10 goals each, and a 55,132-parameter model trained for 200 epochs. These are new experimental settings; the established GridWorld, city-map, iGibson, and heuristic split and resolution protocols remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a focused comparison with and without the PINN loss, including value errors and gradient-residual visualizations in Table 2 and Figure 7. Appendix D.4 also identifies Figure 3 as a best-performing example and adds a worst-performing iGibson example in Figure 9. The obstacle/Deepnorm comparison and erosion sensitivity study already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over maps or instances without seed information, repeated-training-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added results follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds hybrid-loss results, P-NTFields results, and manipulator training/test errors of 0.027/0.041. In Table 2, the new hybrid variant achieves 0.1842 error on 1024^2 city maps alongside the retained PNO value of 0.2034. Figure 3 revises PNO errors from 0.0877 to 0.0771 for Bolton and 0.2363 to 0.2413 for Samuel. Appendix D.3 changes SDF error from 0.064 to 0.068, although Section 4 still reports 0.064; Table 2 changes FMM time from 104.62 to 104.64 ms. Tables 1 and 3–6 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 now defines the previously unspecified theta_v in the continuity bound as the diameter of the value-function space. This is a limited formal clarification. The approximation theorem, consistency lemmas, viscosity results, assumptions, and substantive proof arguments are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list add a claim of optimal planning with 4-DOF manipulators. Contribution (c) drops v1's approximately 20-fold city-map speedup claim. The central operator-learning, generalization, super-resolution, and heuristic-efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 warns that excessive PINN-loss weighting can favor solutions such as the Euclidean norm. It explains why P-NTFields can generate smooth paths despite inaccurate value magnitudes and attributes NTFields failures to local minima. The conclusion adds a proposed ARA* repair pass while removing v1's explicit future-work discussion of real-robot validation and robot dynamics constraints.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a concrete project-code link in place of the deferred-release statement. Appendix D.5 adds MATLAB collision-checking and simulation details, FMM data generation, hardware, and training times; Figure 7 specifies a PINN weight of 0.05 for its example. The iGibson baseline-training account changes from six hours per environment for NTFields to approximately three hours for NTFields/P-NTFields. Some caption-level explanations of timing scope are omitted.

R1.justification: V2 adds Chaplot et al. (2021) and Ni and Qureshi's progressive-learning work, including a discussion of P-NTFields in Appendix D.1. It removes the PINNeik citation by bin Waheed et al. (2021). The broader positioning between neural motion planning and operator learning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 tightens portions of the introduction and related work, expands the layer-level architecture explanation, and revises the experimental narrative and conclusion. Sections 1–6 and Appendices A–E retain their organization, with D.5 added. Author affiliations and conference-header text also change.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially revised: Table 2 gains a hybrid-loss row and ablation labels; Figure 3 adds P-NTFields panels and contour displays; and Figures 4, 7, 9, and 10 introduce manipulator and diagnostic visualizations. The heuristic and GridWorld figures are redrawn, while the Paris and erosion figures are retained and renumbered. The ICLR format also changes typography, margins, and display placement throughout.

improvement.justification: The loss ablation, P-NTFields comparison, worst-case visualization, and manipulator simulation provide a more informative assessment of PNO's capabilities and failures. The concrete code link improves reproducibility guidance. These are useful incremental gains, tempered by the unquantified manipulator-path optimality claim, removal of explicit real-robot/dynamics caveats, and the new disagreement between main-text and appendix SDF errors.
